correctness.rationale: For the stationary multiplier, the nth Fourier coefficient is u_n+b(u_{n-k}+u_{n+k})/2, with positive u_n. The threshold is the supremum of D_n=(u_{|n-k|}+u_{n+k})/u_n. For 0<alpha<1, concavity increases D_n through n=k and strict convexity of its k-step increments decreases D_n thereafter, so the unique maximizers are +/-k. At alpha=1, D_n is constant beyond k and the coefficients vanish on the whole tail; the nonzero 2k-1 consecutive Fourier modes yield precise distinct-point Gram ranks via Vandermonde. For alpha>1, D_n grows without bound, forcing negative coefficients for every b<0. Auxiliary exact rational and numerical code passed 82,183 assertions; finite code tests are not the proof of universal inequalities.

value.rationale: Positive definiteness of signed spectral perturbations is a natural condition for designing legitimate circle covariances. The exact all-harmonic cone identifies a sharp transition from two missing frequencies with strict finite-site definiteness, to finite-rank Poisson degeneration with exact interpolation capacity, to an unavoidable ultraviolet obstruction. The boundary is continuous from below in alpha but discontinuous from above at the classical Poisson index, a mathematically diagnostic feature of damping curvature. This is a natural complete classification rather than a numerical parameter slice.
